generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: METABASE SQL ZERO-DAY ATTACKS COULD HAVE WIDE BLAST RADIUS
Summary: A zero-day SQL injection flaw in Metabase Cloud (CVSS 10, no CVE yet) let an attacker inject SQL into the app database and get admin access, steal database credentials, and export data. Metabase patched cloud instances automatically. Self-hosted users with the /api/session/reset_password endpoint exposed on port 3000 remain vulnerable. n8n confirmed 136 leaked customer records. Kilo Code confirmed exposed Slack tokens and customer data. Metabase told self-hosted users to patch now or block that endpoint, rotate credentials, and revoke sessions.

Editorial idea:
A single exposed entry point can turn a software flaw into a wide compromise.

Central subject:
The exposed Metabase password-reset endpoint and the sensitive systems behind it.

Visual relationship:
A publicly reachable application endpoint connects an attacker to administrative access, database credentials, and exported customer data.

Composition:
Show a secure records room behind a building facade, with one small service entrance left open to the outside; a narrow path through that entrance leads toward filing cabinets and access keys, making the disproportionate blast radius clear.

Permitted literal elements:
An open service entrance
Database records and credential keys inside the secured room
A small external figure approaching the entrance
A closed barrier around the remaining entrances

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
Racks
Chips
Laptops
Robots
Clouds
Shields
Arrows
Charts
Skyscrapers
Chess
Handshakes
Split-screen conflict
Logos
Rendered text

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Making the breach look like a physical burglary with no clear connection to an exposed software path
Showing generic cyber-security imagery instead of the password-reset endpoint and its consequences
Implying that every Metabase deployment was compromised
Adding unsupported details about the attacker or affected organizations

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
